stochastic partial differential equations ( spdes ) , or partial differential equations ( pdes ) with uncertainties , play an important role in many areas of engineering and applied sciences such as turbulence , flows in random media , solid mechanics , filtering , and finance . 
 numerical simulations of spdes are typically based on the monte carlo ( mc ) or the polynomial chaos ( pc ) methods @xcite . in both cases , the long - time simulation of spdes proves to be quite expensive  @xcite . in this paper , we extend the pc - based method developed for stochastic differential equations in @xcite to the setting of spdes . 
 the pc method originates from the works @xcite and enables us to expand ( square integrable ) functionals of brownian motion in a basis of hermite polynomials . 
 applications of such a framework to random flows and turbulence theory are examined in @xcite . 
 more recently , works in @xcite combined the pc method with the karhunen  loeve ( kl ) expansion @xcite to study structural mechanics problems . 
 the generalized polynomial chaos ( gpc ) developed in @xcite next extends the hermite pc to a set of non - gaussian random parameters . 
 the main advantage of the pc method is that it allows us to propagate stochasticity by providing expansions of quantities of interest in terms of appropriate uncertainties while in effect replacing the stochastic equations by systems of deterministic equations . 
 once these deterministic equations are solved , the statistical properties of the solution can be readily inferred from the coefficients of the expansion , which facilitates uncertainty quantification . in some cases , 
 the pc method can propagate uncertainties with a substantially lower cost than mc methods ; especially for low dimensional uncertainties  @xcite ; see also @xcite . 
 however , in cases of high dimensional random parameters , the efficiency of the pc method is reduced because of the large number of terms that appear in the expansion ....

 the long - time simulation of spde solutions by polynomial chaos ( pc ) methods is notoriously difficult as the dimension of the stochastic variables increases linearly with time . exploiting the markovian property of white noise , 
 dgpc @xcite implements a restart procedure that allows us to expand solutions at future times in terms of orthogonal polynomials of the measure describing the solution at a given time and the future white noise . 
 the dimension of the representation is kept minimal by application of a karhunen  loeve ( kl ) expansion . using frequent restarts and low degree polynomials on sparse multi - index sets , 
 the method allows us to perform long time simulations , including the calculation of invariant measures for systems which possess one . 
 we apply the method to the numerical simulation of stochastic burgers and navier stokes equations with white noise forcing . 
 our method also allows us to incorporate time - independent random coefficients such as a random viscosity . 
 we propose several numerical simulations and show that the algorithm compares favorably with standard monte carlo methods .

随着深度神经网络在计算机视觉和自然语言处理等领域取得突破，其参数规模和计算复杂度迅速增长，给模型部署带来了存储、算力和能耗方面的挑战。神经网络剪枝作为一种重要的模型压缩技术，旨在在尽量保持精度的前提下，去除冗余参数或结构，从而提升推理效率。

从方法上看，剪枝策略可分为非结构化剪枝和结构化剪枝。非结构化剪枝通常基于权值幅值、梯度敏感度或泰勒展开近似，直接将不重要的连接置零，压缩率高但对硬件不友好。结构化剪枝则以通道、卷积核或层为单位进行裁剪，更易于加速实际推理。经典方法包括基于L1/L2范数的通道剪枝、网络敏感度分析以及结合正则化项的稀疏化训练。此外，彩票假说提出在过参数化网络中存在可独立训练的稀疏子网络，为迭代剪枝与重训练提供了理论依据。近年来，动态剪枝和自适应阈值策略进一步提升了剪枝过程的稳定性。

在效果上，合理的剪枝策略可显著降低参数量和FLOPs，同时仅带来有限的精度损失，甚至在某些场景下改善泛化性能。总体而言，神经网络剪枝在模型压缩与高效部署中具有重要价值，其与量化、蒸馏等技术的协同应用仍是未来研究的重点方向。

instruction: 将下面这段计算机领域的学术摘要翻译成中文。
input: Knowledge distillation is a model compression and transfer learning technique in which a compact student model is trained to replicate the behavior of a larger, high-capacity teacher model. The core idea is to leverage the rich soft target information encoded in the teacher’s output probability distribution, rather than relying solely on hard labels. By minimizing a distillation loss—commonly the Kullback–Leibler divergence between the student and teacher logits softened by a temperature parameter—the student can capture inter-class similarity and dark knowledge that are not explicit in one-hot annotations. Knowledge distillation can be applied in various settings, including offline distillation with a pretrained teacher, online distillation with jointly trained models, and self-distillation where a model teaches its own smaller variants or intermediate layers. Extensions such as feature-based distillation align intermediate representations using metrics like mean squared error or attention transfer, while relational distillation preserves structural relationships among samples in embedding space. In practice, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in model size, inference latency, and energy consumption with minimal performance degradation, making it particularly valuable for deploying deep neural networks on resource-constrained devices. Furthermore, it has been successfully applied across domains such as computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition, and is increasingly integrated with techniques like quantization and pruning to achieve more efficient and scalable AI systems.
output:
<think>\n\n</think>\n\n知识蒸馏（Knowledge Distillation）是一种模型压缩与迁移学习技术，其核心思想是训练一个结构紧凑的学生模型（student model）来复现一个容量更大、表达能力更强的教师模型（teacher model）的行为。该方法的关键在于利用教师模型输出概率分布中所蕴含的丰富“软目标”（soft targets）信息，而不是仅依赖于硬标签（hard labels）。通过最小化蒸馏损失（distillation loss）——通常为在温度参数（temperature）平滑后的学生与教师 logits 之间的 Kullback–Leibler 散度（KL divergence）——学生模型能够学习到类别之间的相似性以及在 one-hot 标注中未显式体现的“暗知识”（dark knowledge）。

知识蒸馏可应用于多种设置，包括使用预训练教师模型的离线蒸馏（offline distillation）、模型联合训练的在线蒸馏（online distillation），以及模型对自身较小变体或中间层进行教学的自蒸馏（self-distillation）。其扩展形式还包括基于特征的蒸馏（feature-based distillation），通过均方误差（mean squared error）或 attention transfer 等度量方式对齐中间表示；以及关系蒸馏（relational distillation），用于保持嵌入空间中样本之间的结构关系。

在实际应用中，知识蒸馏能够在性能损失极小的前提下显著降低模型规模、推理延迟和能耗，因此在资源受限设备上部署深度神经网络时具有重要价值。此外，该技术已在计算机视觉、自然语言处理和语音识别等多个领域取得成功应用，并且正日益与量化（quantization）和剪枝（pruning）等技术相结合，以构建更加高效、可扩展的人工智能系统。

instruction: 请提炼以下段落的核心思想。
input:
在机器学习与数据挖掘任务中，模型性能往往受限于原始数据质量与表达方式，特征工程因此成为连接数据与算法的关键环节。现实业务数据通常存在维度高、分布不均、噪声与缺失值并存等问题，若直接建模，容易导致过拟合或泛化能力不足。

特征工程的方法可分为特征构造、特征变换与特征选择三类。特征构造强调结合领域知识，通过统计聚合、交互项或时间窗口生成更具判别力的变量；特征变换关注数值尺度与分布形态，常见手段包括标准化、归一化、对数变换以及类别特征的独热编码或目标编码；特征选择则旨在降低维度、减少冗余，可采用过滤法（如信息增益、卡方检验）、包裹法（基于模型性能的递归特征消除）以及嵌入法（如L1正则化、树模型特征重要性）。在高维连续特征场景下，主成分分析等降维技术也能有效压缩信息。

通过系统化的特征工程，可以显著提升模型的收敛速度、稳定性与可解释性。在严格的交叉验证与防止信息泄漏的前提下，优质特征往往比复杂模型结构更能带来性能增益，是构建高可靠性智能系统的基础。

instruction: Help me translate this technical content to Chinese.
input: Model compression and quantization techniques are critical for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments while preserving acceptable accuracy and performance. Model compression encompasses a range of methods, including parameter pruning, low-rank factorization, knowledge distillation, and weight sharing, all aimed at reducing model size and computational complexity. Pruning removes redundant or less significant parameters based on structured or unstructured criteria, whereas low-rank decomposition approximates dense weight matrices with factorized representations to lower memory and FLOP requirements. Quantization further optimizes models by reducing numerical precision, typically converting 32-bit floating-point weights and activations into lower-bit representations such as INT8, INT4, or even binary formats. Post-training quantization and quantization-aware training are two dominant paradigms, with the latter incorporating quantization effects during training to mitigate accuracy degradation. Advanced techniques such as mixed-precision quantization, dynamic range quantization, and hardware-aware quantization exploit the trade-offs between precision, latency, and energy efficiency on specific accelerators. Collectively, these approaches enable efficient inference on edge devices and large-scale systems, while also introducing challenges related to numerical stability, error propagation, and model robustness that require careful algorithmic and hardware co-design.

Machine translation methods have evolved from rule-based machine translation (RBMT) to statistical machine translation (SMT), and further to neural machine translation (NMT). RBMT relies on manually constructed linguistic rules and bilingual dictionaries, which entail high development costs and limited generalization capability. SMT is centered on probabilistic models, maximizing the conditional translation probability through word alignment, phrase modeling, and decoding search. NMT adopts an end-to-end encoder–decoder framework, incorporates attention mechanisms and Transformer architectures, and, together with subword segmentation and large-scale pretraining, significantly enhances semantic representation and long-distance dependency modeling. Translation quality is typically evaluated using automatic metrics such as BLEU.

instruction: 中文翻译：
input: Few-shot learning (FSL) refers to a class of machine learning techniques designed to enable models to generalize effectively from a very limited number of labeled training examples per class. Unlike conventional supervised learning, which relies on large-scale annotated datasets, few-shot learning addresses data scarcity by leveraging prior knowledge, inductive biases, and transferable representations. Core approaches to FSL include metric-based methods, such as Siamese Networks, Prototypical Networks, and Matching Networks, which learn embedding spaces where samples from the same class are clustered closely, enabling classification via distance-based metrics. Another prominent paradigm is optimization-based methods, such as Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML), which aim to learn model parameters that can be rapidly adapted to new tasks with minimal gradient updates. Additionally, memory-augmented neural networks and attention mechanisms are often employed to store and retrieve task-relevant information efficiently. Few-shot learning is closely related to meta-learning, as it typically involves training across a distribution of tasks to acquire transferable learning strategies. The challenges in FSL include overfitting, task distribution shift, and robustness to noisy or ambiguous samples. Recent research has explored the integration of self-supervised pretraining, foundation models, and Bayesian inference to improve uncertainty estimation and generalization performance. Few-shot learning has become increasingly important in domains such as medical imaging, natural language processing, and robotics, where labeled data is expensive, scarce, or difficult to obtain.

instruction: 请提取以下论文片段的核心观点，并进行简要总结。
input:
Image generation models aim to synthesize realistic or semantically meaningful images by learning the underlying distribution of visual data. This problem is fundamental to computer vision and artificial intelligence, with applications in content creation, data augmentation, simulation, medical imaging, and human–computer interaction. The core challenge lies in modeling high-dimensional, multimodal image distributions while maintaining both global coherence and fine-grained detail. Early approaches based on parametric graphics or rule-based systems lacked scalability and generalization, motivating the adoption of data-driven generative models.

Modern image generation is dominated by deep generative models, particularly Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), and diffusion-based models. VAEs formulate image generation as a probabilistic latent-variable problem, optimizing a variational lower bound on the data likelihood. They provide stable training and meaningful latent representations but often suffer from blurry outputs due to the use of pixel-wise reconstruction losses. GANs address this limitation through an adversarial framework, where a generator and discriminator are trained in a minimax game. By implicitly learning the data distribution, GANs can produce sharp and high-fidelity images, though they are prone to training instability, mode collapse, and sensitivity to hyperparameters.

Diffusion models have recently emerged as a dominant paradigm due to their strong performance and training stability. These models define a forward process that gradually adds noise to data and a learned reverse process that denoises samples step by step. By parameterizing the reverse process with deep neural networks, typically U-Net architectures with attention mechanisms, diffusion models achieve state-of-the-art image quality and diversity. Conditioning mechanisms, such as classifier guidance, cross-attention, or text encoders (e.g., CLIP-based embeddings), enable controllable generation and support multimodal tasks like text-to-image synthesis.

Across these approaches, architectural innovations play a critical role. Convolutional neural networks capture local spatial correlations, while transformers and self-attention modules model long-range dependencies and global structure. Training strategies often rely on large-scale datasets, extensive data augmentation, and optimization techniques such as adaptive learning rates and exponential moving averages. Model evaluation remains non-trivial; common quantitative metrics include Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Inception Score (IS), although human perceptual studies are often necessary to assess semantic alignment and visual realism.

In conclusion, image generation models have progressed rapidly, evolving from likelihood-based formulations to adversarial and diffusion-based frameworks with impressive empirical results. Despite these advances, open challenges remain in computational efficiency, controllability, robustness, and ethical considerations such as bias and misuse. Ongoing research continues to explore more scalable architectures, better evaluation protocols, and tighter integration between generative modeling and downstream vision tasks.

instruction: 请对以下内容进行摘要，突出关键信息。
input:
Modern data-intensive systems rely on robust data pipeline design to transform raw, heterogeneous data into reliable, analytics-ready assets. As organizations ingest data from transactional systems, IoT devices, logs, and third-party APIs at increasing scale and velocity, poorly designed pipelines can become a primary source of latency, data quality issues, and operational risk. The core challenge lies in building pipelines that are scalable, fault-tolerant, and evolvable while maintaining strong guarantees around data consistency, observability, and governance.

A well-designed data pipeline typically decomposes the end-to-end flow into ingestion, processing, storage, and serving layers. At the ingestion stage, pipelines must support both batch and streaming data sources. Technologies such as Apache Kafka, Amazon Kinesis, or cloud-native message queues are commonly used to decouple producers and consumers, enabling back-pressure handling and horizontal scalability. Schema management at this stage is critical; adopting schema registries and enforcing schema evolution rules helps prevent downstream breakages and supports backward and forward compatibility.

The processing layer is responsible for data transformation, enrichment, validation, and aggregation. Distributed data processing frameworks such as Apache Spark, Flink, or Beam provide abstractions for parallel execution, state management, and windowed computations. Design decisions here often involve choosing between batch processing, micro-batching, and true stream processing, each with different trade-offs in latency, throughput, and complexity. Idempotent transformations and exactly-once or at-least-once processing semantics are essential considerations to ensure correctness in the presence of retries and partial failures. Additionally, incorporating data quality checks—such as constraint validation, anomaly detection, and deduplication—helps shift error detection earlier in the pipeline.

Storage and serving layers must be optimized for downstream access patterns. Data lakes built on object storage offer cost-effective, scalable storage for raw and curated datasets, while data warehouses and lakehouse architectures provide optimized query performance through columnar storage, indexing, and metadata management. Partitioning strategies, file formats (e.g., Parquet or ORC), and compaction policies have a significant impact on query efficiency and maintenance overhead. Serving layers may also include feature stores or low-latency databases to support machine learning and real-time applications.

Operational concerns are central to pipeline design. Observability mechanisms—such as structured logging, metrics, and distributed tracing—enable proactive monitoring and faster incident response. Workflow orchestration tools like Apache Airflow or cloud-native schedulers help manage dependencies, retries, and backfills. Infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD practices further improve reproducibility and reduce configuration drift across environments.

In conclusion, effective data pipeline design is not solely about moving data from source to sink, but about engineering a resilient, observable, and adaptable system. By applying modular architectures, well-defined contracts, and strong operational practices, organizations can build pipelines that scale with data growth, support advanced analytics and machine learning, and deliver trustworthy data products over time.

instruction: What are the main points of the following content?
input:
Optimization algorithms play a central role in training modern machine learning and deep neural network models, as they directly affect convergence speed, stability, and final generalization performance. Classical first-order methods such as stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and its momentum variants remain widely used due to their simplicity and scalability. However, these methods are sensitive to learning rate selection, suffer from slow convergence in ill-conditioned landscapes, and often struggle with sparse or noisy gradients. As model architectures grow deeper and datasets larger, these limitations motivate continuous improvements to optimizer algorithms.

Recent research has focused on enhancing adaptive optimization methods that dynamically adjust learning rates based on gradient statistics. Algorithms such as AdaGrad, RMSProp, and Adam estimate first- and second-order moments of gradients to perform parameter-wise updates, enabling faster convergence in high-dimensional and sparse settings. Despite their empirical success, adaptive optimizers may exhibit suboptimal generalization and unstable training behavior due to biased moment estimates and excessive adaptivity. To address these issues, several improvements have been proposed, including bias correction techniques, decoupled weight decay, and variance rectification. For example, AdamW separates L2 regularization from gradient-based updates, resulting in more consistent regularization behavior and improved generalization across tasks.

Another important direction is the integration of second-order information without incurring prohibitive computational costs. Approximations such as quasi-Newton methods, diagonal or block-diagonal Hessian estimates, and curvature-aware preconditioning have been explored to capture local geometry more effectively. Optimizers like Shampoo and K-FAC approximate second-order statistics using structured matrix factorizations, significantly accelerating convergence in large-scale neural networks. Additionally, recent methods incorporate low-rank or sketch-based approximations to further reduce memory and computation overhead, making second-order techniques more practical in distributed environments.

Variance reduction and adaptive scheduling strategies also contribute to optimizer improvements. Techniques such as gradient clipping, adaptive learning rate decay, and warmup schedules enhance numerical stability, especially during early training stages. Moreover, combining adaptive optimizers with periodic SGD-style updates or lookahead mechanisms can balance fast initial convergence with strong asymptotic performance. These hybrid approaches exploit the strengths of multiple optimization paradigms while mitigating their individual weaknesses.

Empirical evaluations across vision, language, and reinforcement learning benchmarks demonstrate that improved optimizer algorithms can significantly reduce training time, increase robustness to hyperparameter choices, and yield better generalization performance. In conclusion, optimizer algorithm improvement is an active and impactful research area, where advances in adaptive estimation, curvature approximation, and stability control continue to push the boundaries of efficient and reliable model training.

instruction: 用通俗易懂的语言向初学者解释迁移学习。
output:
<think>\n\n</think>\n\n迁移学习可以理解为：**把已经学会的知识，拿来帮你更快地学新东西。**

打个比方：  
你已经会骑自行车了，再去学骑摩托车就会容易很多。因为你已经懂得**保持平衡、看路、转弯**这些基础技能。迁移学习就是这样——**先学一个任务，再把学到的经验用到另一个相关任务上**。

放到人工智能里：  
假设有一个模型，已经通过大量图片学会了“识别猫和狗”。这个模型其实已经懂了很多**通用的东西**，比如边缘、颜色、形状。现在你想让它学会“识别老虎和狮子”，就不需要从零开始训练，只要在原来的基础上稍微再学一学就行了。这就是迁移学习。

**为什么要用迁移学习？**

迁移学习就是——**先学会一个，再用它来更快学下一个。**

instruction: 阅读下文，用一句话概括其主要贡献。
input:
Large-scale pre-trained models, especially in natural language processing and computer vision, have demonstrated remarkable generalization能力 across diverse tasks. However, fully fine-tuning these models for each downstream task is often prohibitively expensive in terms of computational resources, memory footprint, and deployment cost. As model sizes grow to billions or even trillions of parameters, full fine-tuning also raises practical challenges such as slow iteration cycles, increased risk of overfitting on small datasets, and difficulties in maintaining multiple task-specific model copies. These limitations motivate the need for more efficient adaptation strategies.

Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) addresses this problem by adapting pre-trained models to downstream tasks while updating only a small subset of parameters, or by introducing lightweight task-specific modules. The core idea is to preserve the majority of pre-trained weights in a frozen state and achieve task adaptation through minimal additional parameters. Representative PEFT methods include adapter-based approaches, low-rank adaptation (LoRA), prefix tuning, prompt tuning, and bias-only fine-tuning. Adapter-based methods insert small bottleneck layers between existing layers of the backbone model, enabling task-specific transformations with negligible parameter overhead. LoRA, on the other hand, decomposes weight updates into low-rank matrices, effectively approximating full fine-tuning updates while significantly reducing trainable parameters. Prefix and prompt tuning operate at the input or intermediate representation level by learning continuous task-specific embeddings that steer model behavior without modifying core weights.

From an optimization perspective, PEFT methods reduce the dimensionality of the parameter search space, which can improve training stability and sample efficiency, particularly in low-resource scenarios. They also enable faster convergence and lower GPU memory consumption, making it feasible to adapt large foundation models on commodity hardware. Importantly, PEFT facilitates modularity: multiple task-specific adaptations can coexist by swapping lightweight parameter sets while sharing a common frozen backbone. This property is especially valuable in multi-task and continual learning settings.

Empirical results across benchmarks such as GLUE, SuperGLUE, and various domain-specific tasks show that PEFT methods can achieve performance comparable to, and sometimes indistinguishable from, full fine-tuning, while training only a fraction (often less than 1%) of the total parameters. In addition, PEFT improves deployment efficiency, as only small delta parameters need to be stored, transmitted, or updated. In conclusion, Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning provides a scalable and practical paradigm for adapting large pre-trained models, balancing performance, efficiency, and maintainability, and has become a key component in modern large-model deployment pipelines.

instruction: 请将以下英文内容译为中文，保持专业术语准确。
input: Feature engineering methods constitute a critical stage in the machine learning pipeline, directly influencing model performance, robustness, and interpretability. These methods aim to transform raw data into informative, discriminative, and low-redundancy features that align with the inductive biases of learning algorithms. Common techniques include feature extraction, feature transformation, feature selection, and feature construction. Feature extraction methods, such as principal component analysis (PCA), independent component analysis (ICA), and domain-specific signal or text representations, reduce dimensionality while preserving salient information. Feature transformation techniques, including normalization, standardization, logarithmic scaling, and power transforms, improve numerical stability and convergence behavior during optimization. Feature selection methods—such as filter-based approaches (e.g., mutual information, chi-square tests), wrapper methods (e.g., recursive feature elimination), and embedded methods (e.g., L1 regularization, tree-based importance measures)—aim to eliminate irrelevant or redundant features, thereby reducing overfitting and computational cost. More advanced feature construction approaches leverage interaction terms, polynomial features, or learned representations via deep learning models and representation learning techniques. In recent years, automated feature engineering and representation learning, including autoencoders, embedding models, and feature synthesis frameworks, have gained prominence by reducing manual effort and capturing complex, non-linear relationships. Effective feature engineering requires domain knowledge, statistical insight, and iterative validation, and remains a decisive factor in achieving high-performing and generalizable machine learning systems.

instruction: 将下面这段计算机领域的学术摘要翻译成中文。
input: Gradient clipping is a stabilization technique widely used in training deep neural networks, particularly recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and very deep architectures, to mitigate the problem of exploding gradients. During backpropagation, gradients can grow exponentially with network depth or sequence length, leading to numerical instability, parameter overflow, and divergence of the optimization process. Gradient clipping addresses this issue by enforcing an upper bound on the magnitude of gradients before they are applied in the parameter update step. The two most common approaches are value clipping and norm-based clipping. In value clipping, each component of the gradient vector is clamped to a predefined range, whereas in norm-based clipping, the entire gradient vector is rescaled if its L2 norm exceeds a specified threshold. Formally, for norm-based clipping, if the gradient norm exceeds the threshold, the gradient is multiplied by the ratio of the threshold to the actual norm, preserving its direction while limiting its magnitude. This approach is generally preferred, as it maintains the relative proportions among gradient components. Gradient clipping interacts closely with optimization algorithms such as stochastic gradient descent, Adam, and RMSProp, and is often used in conjunction with learning rate scheduling. While gradient clipping does not address vanishing gradients, it significantly improves training robustness, enables the use of higher learning rates, and enhances convergence stability in complex, non-convex optimization landscapes.
output:
<think>\n\n</think>\n\n梯度裁剪（Gradient clipping）是一种在训练深度神经网络时广泛使用的稳定化技术，尤其常见于循环神经网络（RNNs）和非常深的网络结构中，用于缓解梯度爆炸问题。在反向传播过程中，梯度可能随着网络深度或序列长度呈指数级增长，从而导致数值不稳定、参数溢出以及优化过程发散。梯度裁剪通过在参数更新之前对梯度的幅值施加上界来解决这一问题。

最常见的两种方法是值裁剪（value clipping）和基于范数的裁剪（norm-based clipping）。在值裁剪中，梯度向量的每一个分量都会被限制在预先定义的区间内；而在基于范数的裁剪中，如果整个梯度向量的 L2 范数超过给定阈值，则对梯度进行整体缩放。形式化地说，在基于范数的裁剪中，当梯度范数大于阈值时，将梯度乘以“阈值与实际范数之比”，在限制其幅值的同时保持梯度方向不变。由于该方法能够维持各梯度分量之间的相对比例，因此通常更为常用。

梯度裁剪与随机梯度下降（stochastic gradient descent）、Adam、RMSProp 等优化算法密切配合，并且常与学习率调度策略联合使用。尽管梯度裁剪并不能解决梯度消失问题，但它能够显著提升训练过程的鲁棒性，支持使用更高的学习率，并在复杂的非凸优化环境中增强收敛稳定性。

GPU parallel computing has become a cornerstone of modern high-performance computing due to the growing demand for processing massive data sets and executing computationally intensive algorithms. Traditional CPU-based architectures are optimized for low-latency execution of sequential tasks, but they struggle to efficiently exploit data-level parallelism at large scale. As applications in scientific simulation, deep learning, computer vision, and big data analytics continue to expand, the limitations of serial and coarse-grained parallel processing have motivated the widespread adoption of GPU-based solutions.

The fundamental advantage of GPUs lies in their massively parallel architecture. A GPU consists of thousands of lightweight cores organized into streaming multiprocessors, designed to execute the same instruction across multiple data elements simultaneously under the Single Instruction, Multiple Threads (SIMT) model. Programming frameworks such as CUDA and OpenCL expose this architecture to developers by allowing kernels to be launched across a large number of threads, grouped into warps and thread blocks. Effective GPU programming requires careful consideration of memory hierarchy, including global memory, shared memory, registers, and caches, as memory access patterns often dominate overall performance.

To fully leverage GPU parallelism, algorithms must be reformulated to maximize parallel workload and minimize synchronization overhead. Data decomposition is a common strategy, where large problems are partitioned into independent or semi-independent subproblems that can be processed concurrently. Techniques such as memory coalescing, minimizing branch divergence, and overlapping computation with data transfer via asynchronous execution are essential for achieving high throughput. Furthermore, recent advances in unified memory and hardware-managed caching have simplified development while still allowing fine-grained performance tuning when necessary.

The impact of GPU parallel computing is evident across multiple domains. In deep learning, GPUs dramatically accelerate training and inference by parallelizing matrix multiplications and convolution operations. In scientific computing, simulations involving fluid dynamics, molecular dynamics, and climate modeling benefit from orders-of-magnitude speedups compared to CPU-only implementations. Additionally, GPUs have enabled real-time data processing in areas such as video encoding, signal processing, and financial modeling, where latency and throughput are critical constraints.

In conclusion, GPU parallel computing addresses the fundamental scalability challenges posed by modern computational workloads. By exploiting massive parallelism and high memory bandwidth, GPUs provide a powerful platform for accelerating data-intensive applications. While effective utilization requires specialized programming models and performance-aware design, ongoing improvements in hardware architecture, software ecosystems, and compiler technology continue to lower the barrier to entry. As a result, GPU parallel computing is expected to remain a central component of high-performance and AI-driven systems in the foreseeable future.

In-Context Learning (ICL) refers to the capability of large language models to directly adapt to new tasks during inference through examples and instructions provided in the prompt, without updating model parameters. Research indicates that ICL relies on self-attention to induce patterns from contextual examples, exhibiting meta-learning-like behavior, and may be equivalent to performing approximate implicit gradient or Bayesian updates in a latent space. Current work focuses on mechanism interpretability, generalization boundaries, and its synergy with fine-tuning.

input: Data pipeline design is a critical discipline in modern data-intensive systems, focusing on the reliable, scalable, and maintainable movement of data from heterogeneous sources to downstream consumers. A well-architected pipeline typically supports both batch and streaming workloads, leveraging ETL or ELT patterns depending on computational and latency requirements. Core design considerations include schema management and evolution, ensuring backward and forward compatibility as source systems change. Robust data quality checks—such as validation, deduplication, and anomaly detection—should be embedded at multiple stages to prevent the propagation of corrupt or inconsistent data. From a systems perspective, pipelines must be fault-tolerant and idempotent, often employing exactly-once or at-least-once processing semantics to handle retries and partial failures. Scalability is achieved through horizontal partitioning, efficient storage formats (e.g., Parquet or ORC), and distributed processing frameworks. Orchestration tools coordinate task dependencies, scheduling, and recovery, while observability mechanisms—metrics, logs, and tracing—enable operational insight and performance tuning. Additionally, effective pipeline design incorporates metadata management, data lineage tracking, and governance controls to ensure security, compliance, and reproducibility. Together, these principles enable pipelines to serve as dependable backbones for analytics, machine learning, and real-time decision-making systems.

数据流水线设计是现代数据密集型系统中的一项关键学科，关注于将来自异构数据源的数据以可靠、可扩展且易维护的方式传输到下游消费者。一个架构良好的流水线通常同时支持批处理和流处理工作负载，并根据计算需求和时延要求选择采用 ETL 或 ELT 模式。核心设计考量包括模式（schema）管理与演进，以确保在源系统发生变化时保持向后和向前兼容性。健壮的数据质量检查——如数据校验、去重和异常检测——应嵌入在多个阶段，以防止损坏或不一致数据的传播。从系统角度来看，流水线必须具备容错性和幂等性，通常通过“恰好一次”（exactly-once）或“至少一次”（at-least-once）的处理语义来应对重试和部分失败。可扩展性通过水平分区、高效的存储格式（如 Parquet 或 ORC）以及分布式处理框架来实现。编排工具负责协调任务依赖、调度和故障恢复，而可观测性机制——包括指标、日志和追踪——则提供运行洞察和性能调优能力。此外，高效的流水线设计还应纳入元数据管理、数据血缘追踪以及治理控制，以确保安全性、合规性和可复现性。综合这些原则，数据流水线能够作为分析、机器学习和实时决策系统的可靠基础支撑。

instruction: Briefly summarize the following passage.
input:
在深度学习模型不断增大的背景下，高精度模型往往伴随高计算与存储成本，难以在边缘设备或低时延场景中部署。知识蒸馏（Knowledge Distillation）通过模型压缩的方式，在保持性能的同时降低复杂度，成为连接模型性能与工程落地的重要技术路径。

知识蒸馏的核心思想是教师—学生框架：利用性能更强的教师模型指导轻量学生模型训练。经典方法基于响应蒸馏，即让学生模型拟合教师模型输出的软标签（soft targets），通常通过引入温度系数对logits进行平滑，并最小化学生输出与教师输出之间的KL散度。在此基础上，研究进一步提出特征蒸馏，通过对齐中间层表示、注意力映射或关系矩阵来传递结构化知识；同时，自蒸馏与在线蒸馏等变体缓解了对预训练大模型的依赖，提高训练效率与稳定性。

实践表明，合理设计蒸馏目标与损失权重，可以在显著减少参数量和推理延迟的前提下，使学生模型接近甚至匹配教师模型的泛化性能。知识蒸馏已广泛应用于计算机视觉、语音识别与自然语言处理等领域，是模型压缩与高效推理中的关键技术之一。

input: 知识蒸馏（Knowledge Distillation）是一种模型压缩与性能迁移技术，其核心思想是利用高性能的教师模型（Teacher Model）指导轻量级学生模型（Student Model）的训练。该方法通过引入软标签（Soft Targets），使学生模型不仅学习真实标签的硬决策信息，还能吸收教师模型在类别分布、特征表示及决策边界上的隐含知识。典型做法是在损失函数中结合交叉熵损失与蒸馏损失，后者通常基于温度系数调节后的Softmax输出计算KL散度。知识蒸馏已从最初的分类任务扩展到目标检测、语义分割和大规模语言模型压缩等场景，在降低模型参数量和推理延迟的同时，尽可能保持甚至提升模型泛化能力。

Knowledge Distillation is a model compression and performance transfer technique whose core idea is to use a high-performance teacher model to guide the training of a lightweight student model. By introducing soft targets, the student model learns not only the hard decision information from ground-truth labels but also the implicit knowledge of the teacher model in terms of class distributions, feature representations, and decision boundaries. A typical approach combines cross-entropy loss with a distillation loss in the objective function, where the latter is usually computed as the Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence between temperature-scaled Softmax outputs. Knowledge distillation has expanded from its initial application in classification tasks to scenarios such as object detection, semantic segmentation, and large-scale language model compression, enabling reductions in model parameter count and inference latency while maintaining or even improving generalization performance.

instruction: Briefly summarize the following passage.
input:
Hallucination refers to the tendency of large language models (LLMs) and other generative systems to produce content that is syntactically fluent but factually incorrect, logically inconsistent, or unsupported by the underlying data. This problem is especially critical in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, law, and scientific research, where incorrect statements can lead to severe consequences. From a technical perspective, hallucinations arise from a combination of factors, including imperfect training data, objective functions that prioritize likelihood over factuality, limited grounding in external knowledge, and distributional shifts between training and inference. As model scale and deployment scope increase, hallucination has become a central challenge for trustworthy artificial intelligence.

Several categories of hallucination have been identified in the literature. Intrinsic hallucinations occur when a model contradicts the provided input or context, while extrinsic hallucinations introduce unverifiable or nonexistent facts beyond the input. In sequence-to-sequence and decoder-only architectures, exposure bias and autoregressive error accumulation further amplify these issues. Moreover, maximum likelihood estimation encourages models to generate the most probable continuation rather than the most accurate one, leading to overconfident outputs even under epistemic uncertainty.

Mitigation strategies can be broadly divided into data-centric, model-centric, and inference-time approaches. Data-centric methods focus on improving the quality, diversity, and factual consistency of training corpora, as well as incorporating human feedback through techniques such as reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). Model-centric approaches include architectural modifications, such as integrating symbolic reasoning modules, confidence estimation heads, or uncertainty-aware training objectives. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a particularly effective paradigm, grounding model outputs in external knowledge bases or document collections and thereby reducing reliance on parametric memory alone.

Inference-time techniques further complement these methods. Constrained decoding, factuality-aware reranking, and self-consistency sampling aim to reduce erroneous generations by filtering or aggregating multiple candidate outputs. Post-generation verification, using either rule-based checkers or auxiliary models trained for fact checking, provides an additional layer of defense. More recently, approaches such as self-reflection and chain-of-thought verification encourage models to explicitly reason about the validity of their own responses, improving calibration between confidence and correctness.

Empirical evaluations demonstrate that no single method fully eliminates hallucination, but combined strategies can significantly reduce its frequency and severity. Metrics such as factual precision, faithfulness scores, and human evaluation remain essential for assessing progress, as traditional perplexity-based measures are insufficient. In conclusion, hallucination is a systemic issue rooted in both data and modeling assumptions. Effective mitigation requires a holistic framework that integrates better data curation, grounded model architectures, and robust inference-time validation, ultimately advancing the reliability and safety of generative AI systems.

视觉Transformer（Vision Transformer, ViT）的提出源于卷积神经网络在建模全局依赖关系方面的局限。传统CNN依赖局部感受野和权值共享，具有较强的归纳偏置，但在大尺度上下文建模上受限。随着大规模数据与算力的发展，研究者尝试将在自然语言处理领域表现突出的Transformer结构引入视觉任务，以统一的自注意力机制建模图像中的长程依赖。

ViT的核心思想是将输入图像划分为固定大小的patch，并通过线性投影映射为patch embedding，再叠加位置编码以保留空间信息。这些序列化的视觉token被送入标准的Transformer Encoder，由多头自注意力和前馈网络堆叠而成，从而实现全局特征交互。在分类任务中，通常引入[class] token并通过MLP Head输出预测结果。相较CNN，ViT弱化了先验结构假设，但计算复杂度随token数量呈二次增长，因此在高分辨率场景中需要层次化设计，如Swin Transformer以窗口注意力降低复杂度。

实验表明，在大规模预训练数据支持下，视觉Transformer在图像分类、目标检测和语义分割等任务上取得了与甚至超越CNN的性能。同时，其特征具有更好的可迁移性和模型可扩展性。然而，ViT对数据规模较为敏感，小数据场景下易过拟合，促使后续研究探索卷积与Transformer的混合架构。总体而言，视觉Transformer为视觉建模提供了一种通用且可扩展的新范式。

Mock *interviews* with peers or mentors can be incredibly helpful in building confidence and refining your responses. It's also important to prepare questions to ask the interviewer, as this shows your engagement and interest in the company. ***

Lastly, don't underestimate the importance of non-technical preparation. Dress professionally, arrive on time, and bring extra copies of your resume. During the *interview*, maintain eye contact, listen carefully, and ask clarifying questions when needed. instruction: 概括下文的主要内容和贡献。
input:
Multimodal learning addresses the problem of building models that can jointly reason over heterogeneous data sources such as text, images, audio, video, and structured signals. In many real-world applications, information is distributed across modalities with complementary and redundant cues. For example, visual content provides spatial and semantic context, while language conveys high-level intent and temporal structure. Traditional unimodal models are limited in their capacity to capture such cross-modal dependencies, leading to suboptimal generalization and brittle behavior under distribution shifts. Multimodal learning aims to overcome these limitations by learning shared and modality-specific representations that enable integrated perception and decision-making.

A central challenge in multimodal learning is representation alignment and fusion. Modalities differ in dimensionality, noise characteristics, and temporal resolution, making naive concatenation ineffective. Early fusion methods combine raw or low-level features before model inference, which can capture fine-grained interactions but are sensitive to missing or noisy modalities. Late fusion aggregates modality-specific predictions, offering robustness at the cost of limited cross-modal interaction. Hybrid approaches, including intermediate fusion, attempt to balance these trade-offs by integrating features at multiple layers. Recent advances favor neural architectures based on transformers, where cross-attention mechanisms explicitly model inter-modal dependencies by allowing one modality to attend to another in a shared latent space.

Another key methodological direction is multimodal pretraining using large-scale, weakly supervised data. Contrastive learning objectives, such as aligning image and text embeddings via noise-contrastive estimation, have proven effective for learning semantically meaningful representations without dense annotations. These approaches optimize cross-modal similarity while preserving intra-modal structure, enabling zero-shot and few-shot transfer to downstream tasks. Additionally, techniques such as modality dropout, gated fusion, and mixture-of-experts are employed to handle missing or unreliable modalities at inference time. For temporally structured data, sequence modeling with synchronized encoders and temporal attention is used to capture cross-modal dynamics.

The effectiveness of multimodal learning is demonstrated across a wide range of tasks, including visual question answering, speech recognition with visual context, video understanding, and embodied AI. Empirical results on standardized benchmarks show consistent improvements over unimodal baselines, particularly in scenarios requiring disambiguation or reasoning under uncertainty. Moreover, multimodal models exhibit improved robustness and generalization by leveraging complementary signals, reducing reliance on spurious correlations present in a single modality.

In conclusion, multimodal learning provides a principled framework for integrating heterogeneous data through aligned representations and adaptive fusion strategies. Ongoing research focuses on scaling multimodal pretraining, improving interpretability of cross-modal interactions, and addressing efficiency and bias concerns. As multimodal data becomes increasingly prevalent, these methods are expected to play a critical role in building more capable and reliable artificial intelligence systems.

在实践层面，MLOps 通常以流水线化为核心方法。通过数据版本控制（如特征仓库、数据血缘）、模型训练与评估自动化、以及基于 CI/CD 的模型发布流程，可以实现可重复的训练与快速迭代。同时，引入模型注册中心、在线/离线监控与漂移检测机制，对模型精度、延迟和数据分布进行持续观测，并结合 A/B 测试或灰度发布降低上线风险。

实施 MLOps 后，组织能够显著缩短模型交付周期，提高模型可解释性与可维护性，并在面对数据变化时快速回滚或重训模型。总体来看，MLOps 是连接算法研发与业务价值的关键工程体系，是规模化应用人工智能不可或缺的基础能力。

input:
情感分析是自然语言处理领域的重要研究方向，旨在从文本中自动识别主观态度、情绪倾向与情感强度。随着社交媒体、电商评论和舆情数据的爆炸式增长，传统基于规则和词典的方法在复杂语境、讽刺表达和领域迁移方面逐渐暴露出局限性，难以满足实际应用对准确性和鲁棒性的要求。

当前主流方案以监督学习和深度学习模型为核心。早期方法通常基于特征工程，将情感词频、n-gram、句法依存等特征输入到SVM或逻辑回归模型中。近年来，分布式表示和预训练模型显著提升了性能，词向量如Word2Vec和GloVe缓解了语义稀疏问题，而以Transformer为基础的BERT、RoBERTa等模型通过自注意力机制建模长程依赖，在情感极性分类、多分类及细粒度情感分析任务中表现突出。同时，引入领域自适应微调、多任务学习和情感词增强策略，有助于降低标注成本并提升跨领域泛化能力。

在实验评估方面，情感分析系统通常采用准确率、召回率和F1值作为指标。大量实证结果表明，预训练模型在公开数据集和真实业务场景中均显著优于传统方法。总体来看，情感分析算法正朝着更高语义理解能力和更强可解释性方向演进，为舆情监测、智能客服和推荐系统提供了可靠的技术支撑。

在机器学习建模过程中，过拟合与欠拟合是影响模型泛化性能的两类核心问题。欠拟合通常源于模型复杂度不足或特征表达能力有限，导致模型无法捕捉数据中的真实分布规律，在训练集和测试集上均表现不佳；而过拟合则表现为模型对训练数据拟合过度，学习到了噪声和偶然模式，虽然训练误差很低，但在未见样本上的预测性能显著下降。

从方法层面看，欠拟合常通过提升模型容量或信息量来缓解，例如引入更高阶特征、采用非线性模型、降低正则化强度或延长训练轮次。相反，过拟合的控制更依赖于正则化技术和结构约束，包括L1/L2正则化、Dropout、早停策略以及模型剪枝等。此外，数据层面的手段同样关键，如扩充训练数据规模、进行数据增强或采用交叉验证来稳定模型评估。

在实践中，偏差-方差权衡为理解两者提供了统一视角：欠拟合对应高偏差低方差，过拟合则体现为低偏差高方差。通过系统调节模型复杂度并结合验证集性能进行超参数搜索，可以在两者之间取得平衡。总体而言，合理识别并应对过拟合与欠拟合，是提升模型泛化能力和工程可用性的关键步骤。

What is quantum mechanics, and how does it fundamentally differ from classical physics?
output:
<think>\n\n</think>\n\n<<Understanding the Basics of Quantum Mechanics>>

Quantum mechanics is a fundamental theory in physics that provides a description of the physical properties of nature at the scale of atoms and subatomic particles. In contrast to classical physics, which describes the behavior of objects in a deterministic and continuous manner, quantum mechanics introduces a probabilistic framework. This theory posits that particles can exist in multiple states simultaneously, a phenomenon known as superposition. For example, an electron in an atom can be in multiple energy levels at the same time until it is observed or measured.

One of the key concepts in quantum mechanics is the wavefunction, a mathematical function that describes the quantum state of a system. The wavefunction encodes all the information about the system, including the probabilities of different outcomes when measurements are made. The square of the wavefunction’s amplitude gives the probability density of finding a particle at a particular location.

Another important concept is quantum entanglement, where particles become interconnected in such a way that the state of one particle cannot be described independently of the state of the others, no matter how far apart they are. This phenomenon challenges the classical notion of locality, where objects are only directly influenced by their immediate surroundings.

Entropy also plays a crucial role in quantum mechanics, particularly in the study of quantum systems at thermal equilibrium. The second law of thermodynamics, which states that entropy in a closed system tends to increase over time, has profound implications in quantum systems, influencing the behavior of particles and the evolution of quantum states.

Quantum mechanics fundamentally differs from classical physics in several ways. Firstly, in classical physics, the state of a system is described by precise values of position and momentum. However, in quantum mechanics, these values are described by probabilities. This probabilistic nature is encapsulated in the Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle, which states that the more precisely the position of a particle is known, the less precisely its momentum can be known, and vice versa.

Moreover, quantum mechanics introduces the concept of quantum tunneling, where particles can pass through potential barriers even if they do not have enough energy to classically overcome them. This phenomenon has significant applications in technologies such as semiconductor devices and quantum computing.

The measurement problem in quantum mechanics is another area where it diverges from classical physics. In classical physics, measurement is a passive process that does not affect the system being measured. However, in quantum mechanics, the act of measurement itself can alter the state of the system, leading to the collapse of the wavefunction.

Quantum mechanics also predicts the existence of quantum fields, which are the fundamental entities that give rise to particles. These fields are described by quantum field theory, a framework that combines quantum mechanics with special relativity. Quantum field theory has been incredibly successful in explaining the interactions of particles at high energies, such as those observed in particle accelerators.

In summary, quantum mechanics provides a radically different perspective on the nature of reality compared to classical physics. It introduces concepts such as superposition, wavefunctions, and entanglement, which challenge our classical intuitions and offer a deeper understanding of the behavior of matter and energy at the quantum scale.

instruction: 简要总结以下技术文章的核心论点。
input:
Sentiment analysis algorithms aim to automatically identify and quantify subjective information expressed in text, such as opinions, emotions, and attitudes. With the rapid growth of user-generated content on social media, e-commerce platforms, and online forums, sentiment analysis has become a core task in natural language processing (NLP). It supports downstream applications including brand monitoring, recommendation systems, financial forecasting, and public opinion analysis. The primary challenge lies in modeling the complexity of human language, which involves ambiguity, context dependence, sarcasm, and domain-specific semantics.

Early approaches to sentiment analysis were predominantly lexicon-based. These methods rely on predefined sentiment dictionaries that assign polarity scores to words or phrases. Sentiment polarity of a document is computed by aggregating the scores of matched terms, often with heuristic rules for negation and intensification. While lexicon-based methods are interpretable and require no labeled data, they suffer from limited coverage and poor adaptability to new domains. They also struggle with contextual sentiment shifts and compositional semantics.

Supervised machine learning approaches significantly improved performance by learning sentiment patterns from labeled data. Traditional models such as Naïve Bayes, Support Vector Machines, and Logistic Regression represent text using features like bag-of-words, n-grams, or TF-IDF vectors. These methods capture statistical correlations between lexical features and sentiment labels, achieving robust results on benchmark datasets. However, they depend heavily on feature engineering and fail to model long-range dependencies and semantic relationships.

Recent advances in deep learning have transformed sentiment analysis. Neural architectures such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), particularly Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, learn distributed representations of text via word embeddings. These models can capture syntactic and semantic patterns more effectively than traditional methods. The current state of the art is dominated by transformer-based models, including BERT, RoBERTa, and GPT-style architectures. By leveraging self-attention mechanisms and large-scale pretraining on unlabeled corpora, transformers provide contextualized embeddings that adapt word meaning to surrounding context, enabling fine-grained sentiment classification and aspect-based sentiment analysis.

Model performance is typically evaluated using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score on standard datasets like IMDb, SST, or SemEval benchmarks. Empirical results consistently show that pretrained transformer models fine-tuned on task-specific data outperform earlier approaches, especially in handling nuanced sentiment and contextual polarity. Nevertheless, challenges remain, including data bias, domain transferability, computational cost, and explainability.

In conclusion, sentiment analysis algorithms have evolved from rule-based systems to sophisticated deep learning models that leverage large-scale data and contextual representations. While modern approaches achieve high accuracy, future research is expected to focus on efficiency, robustness across domains, low-resource learning, and interpretable sentiment modeling to support trustworthy real-world applications.

instruction: 请对以下内容进行摘要，突出关键信息。
input:
Federated learning has emerged as a distributed machine learning paradigm designed to address the growing tension between data-driven model performance and data privacy, ownership, and regulatory compliance. In many real-world scenarios such as mobile devices, healthcare systems, and financial institutions, sensitive data cannot be centralized due to legal constraints, security risks, or communication costs. Traditional centralized training approaches require aggregating raw data on a central server, which increases exposure to data breaches and violates privacy-preserving principles. Federated learning reframes this problem by enabling collaborative model training without direct data sharing, thereby aligning machine learning workflows with privacy-by-design requirements.

In a typical federated learning setting, a central coordinator initializes a global model and distributes it to a large number of participating clients, such as smartphones or edge devices. Each client performs local training using its private dataset and computes model updates, commonly in the form of gradients or model weight deltas. Instead of transmitting raw data, clients send these updates back to the server, which aggregates them using algorithms such as Federated Averaging (FedAvg). The aggregated update is then used to refine the global model, and the process iterates over multiple communication rounds. This decentralized optimization framework significantly reduces data exposure while leveraging the statistical strength of distributed datasets.

Federated learning introduces several technical challenges that distinguish it from conventional distributed training. Data across clients is often non-IID (non-independent and identically distributed), leading to model divergence and slower convergence. System heterogeneity, including varying computational capabilities, network latency, and client availability, further complicates synchronous training. To address these issues, advanced optimization techniques, such as adaptive learning rates, partial client participation, and personalized federated models, have been proposed. Additionally, communication efficiency is a critical concern; techniques like model compression, quantization, and sparse updates are widely used to reduce bandwidth consumption.

From a security and privacy perspective, federated learning is often combined with cryptographic and statistical safeguards. Secure aggregation protocols ensure that the server cannot inspect individual client updates, while differential privacy mechanisms add calibrated noise to prevent inference attacks on individual data points. Despite these protections, federated learning remains vulnerable to threats such as model poisoning and backdoor attacks, motivating ongoing research into robust aggregation methods and anomaly detection strategies.

Empirical results across domains demonstrate that federated learning can achieve performance comparable to centralized training while significantly improving data governance and privacy compliance. Its adoption by large-scale systems, including mobile keyboard prediction and medical imaging analysis, highlights its practical viability. In conclusion, federated learning represents a foundational shift toward privacy-aware, decentralized artificial intelligence, offering a scalable solution for collaborative model training in data-sensitive environments.

instruction: 阅读下文，用一句话概括其主要贡献。
input:
Edge inference refers to the execution of machine learning or deep learning models directly on edge devices, such as IoT sensors, mobile phones, industrial controllers, or embedded systems, rather than relying on centralized cloud infrastructure. The motivation for edge inference arises from several practical challenges in cloud-centric AI systems, including high network latency, limited bandwidth, privacy concerns, and unreliable connectivity. In latency-sensitive applications such as autonomous driving, industrial automation, smart healthcare, and real-time video analytics, the delay caused by transmitting data to the cloud and waiting for inference results can be unacceptable. Moreover, transmitting raw data, especially personal or mission-critical data, introduces security and regulatory risks.

To address these challenges, edge inference architectures push trained models closer to the data source. A typical workflow involves training large-scale models in the cloud using abundant computational resources and datasets, followed by model optimization and deployment to edge devices for inference. Key enabling techniques include model compression, quantization, pruning, and knowledge distillation. Quantization reduces numerical precision (e.g., from FP32 to INT8) to lower memory footprint and improve inference throughput, while pruning removes redundant parameters to reduce computational complexity. Knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from a large “teacher” model to a smaller “student” model that is more suitable for edge execution. In addition, hardware-aware optimization is critical, as edge inference often targets heterogeneous accelerators such as NPUs, TPUs, GPUs, and custom ASICs.

From a system perspective, edge inference often operates within a collaborative edge–cloud framework. The cloud handles model training, global optimization, and orchestration, while the edge performs low-latency inference and sometimes lightweight online learning or adaptation. Techniques such as model partitioning and split inference allow parts of a neural network to run on the edge and the remainder in the cloud, balancing latency, energy consumption, and accuracy. Containerization and lightweight runtime frameworks, such as TensorRT, ONNX Runtime, and TVM, further simplify deployment across diverse edge platforms.

The effectiveness of edge inference is typically evaluated in terms of latency reduction, bandwidth savings, energy efficiency, and inference accuracy. Empirical results across multiple domains show that edge inference can reduce end-to-end latency by orders of magnitude and significantly lower network traffic, while maintaining accuracy comparable to cloud-based inference when models are properly optimized. In conclusion, edge inference represents a critical paradigm for scalable and intelligent systems at the network edge. As model architectures, optimization techniques, and edge hardware continue to evolve, edge inference will play an increasingly central role in enabling real-time, privacy-preserving, and cost-efficient AI applications.

instruction: 请把以下技术文档翻译成中文。
input: Feature engineering methods play a critical role in the performance and generalization capability of machine learning models by transforming raw data into informative, discriminative, and model-compatible representations. These methods typically encompass feature extraction, feature transformation, feature selection, and feature construction. Feature extraction focuses on deriving meaningful attributes from unstructured or high-dimensional data, such as using statistical descriptors for time-series signals, n-grams or embeddings for textual data, and convolutional filters for image data. Feature transformation aims to improve data distributions and relationships through techniques such as normalization, standardization, logarithmic scaling, power transforms, and kernel-based mappings, which can enhance model convergence and numerical stability. Feature selection methods, including filter-based approaches (e.g., mutual information, chi-square tests), wrapper methods (e.g., recursive feature elimination), and embedded techniques (e.g., L1 regularization, tree-based importance scores), are used to reduce dimensionality, mitigate overfitting, and improve interpretability by retaining only the most relevant variables. Feature construction further enriches the feature space by generating higher-order interactions, polynomial features, or domain-specific composite indicators. In modern machine learning pipelines, automated feature engineering frameworks and representation learning methods, such as deep neural networks and autoencoders, have gained prominence by learning hierarchical and task-adaptive features directly from data. Nonetheless, domain knowledge–driven feature engineering remains indispensable, particularly in scenarios with limited data, strict interpretability requirements, or high-stakes decision-making contexts.

<think>\n\n</think>\n\n自监督学习是一种介于监督学习与无监督学习之间的机器学习范式。它的核心思想是：不依赖人工标注的数据，而是从原始数据本身构造“伪标签”，通过设计预测任务来训练模型，从而学习有用的表示。

在自监督学习中，数据的结构或内在关系被用来生成学习信号。例如，在计算机视觉中，模型可能被要求预测被遮挡的图像区域、判断两张图片是否来自同一原图，或学习不同数据增强下的一致性表示；在自然语言处理中，常见做法包括预测被掩盖的词语或判断句子之间的顺序关系。这些任务不需要人工标注，却能迫使模型理解数据的语义和结构。

自监督学习的优势在于能够充分利用海量未标注数据，降低对标注成本的依赖，并提升模型在下游任务（如分类、检测、翻译等）中的性能。近年来，它已成为深度学习研究中的重要方向，并在视觉、语言、语音等多个领域展现出强大的潜力。

instruction: 请对以下内容进行摘要，突出关键信息。
input:
The rapid progress of computer vision over the past decade has been largely driven by convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which exploit local receptive fields and weight sharing to model spatial hierarchies efficiently. However, CNNs are inherently biased toward locality and struggle to capture long-range dependencies without deep stacking or complex architectural modifications. At the same time, Transformer architectures, originally developed for natural language processing, have demonstrated remarkable capability in modeling global contextual relationships through self-attention mechanisms. This contrast motivated the exploration of Transformer-based models for visual understanding, leading to the emergence of the Vision Transformer (ViT).

The core idea of the Vision Transformer is to reinterpret an image as a sequence of tokens, analogous to words in a sentence. An input image is first divided into a fixed number of non-overlapping patches, typically of size 16×16 or 14×14 pixels. Each patch is flattened and linearly projected into a latent embedding space, forming a sequence of patch embeddings. To preserve spatial information that is otherwise lost in this tokenization process, learnable or fixed positional embeddings are added to the patch representations. The resulting sequence is then processed by a standard Transformer encoder composed of multi-head self-attention (MHSA) layers and position-wise feed-forward networks, along with residual connections and layer normalization.

Self-attention enables each patch token to attend to all other patches in the image, allowing the model to capture global context and long-range interactions in a single layer. This property contrasts with CNNs, where such interactions emerge only after multiple convolutional layers. For image-level classification, a special learnable class token is prepended to the sequence, and its final representation is used as the global image descriptor. For dense prediction tasks such as segmentation or detection, patch-level representations can be reshaped and decoded through task-specific heads.

Empirical results have shown that Vision Transformers can achieve state-of-the-art performance on large-scale benchmarks such as ImageNet when trained on sufficiently large datasets. Compared to CNNs, ViTs often exhibit better scalability with model size and benefit more from increased data and compute. Moreover, the attention maps produced by ViTs offer a degree of interpretability, as they explicitly model relationships between distant image regions. However, a key limitation is their data inefficiency: without strong inductive biases like locality and translation equivariance, ViTs tend to underperform CNNs in low-data regimes. This issue has led to hybrid architectures and improved variants, such as hierarchical Transformers and convolutional tokenizers, which aim to combine the strengths of both paradigms.

In conclusion, Vision Transformers represent a significant shift in visual representation learning by replacing convolution with self-attention as the primary modeling mechanism. While challenges remain in terms of efficiency and data requirements, ViTs have established a flexible and powerful framework that continues to influence modern computer vision research and applications.

instruction: 请提取以下论文片段的核心观点，并进行简要总结。
input:
在监督学习中，过拟合与欠拟合是影响模型泛化性能的核心问题。欠拟合通常源于模型容量不足或特征表达能力有限，导致训练误差和测试误差同时偏高，体现为高偏差；过拟合则发生在模型过于复杂、对训练数据中的噪声和偶然模式进行学习时，训练误差很低但测试误差显著升高，表现为高方差。这两者本质上体现了偏差—方差权衡。

针对欠拟合问题，常见方法包括提升模型复杂度、引入更具判别力的特征、采用非线性模型或集成学习等；而缓解过拟合则需要控制模型自由度，例如通过正则化（L1/L2 正则）、参数约束、特征选择、数据增强以及降低模型容量。交叉验证可用于稳定评估模型泛化误差，避免因数据划分带来的评估偏差。

在训练过程中，学习曲线是诊断过拟合与欠拟合的重要工具。若训练与验证误差均较高，通常指向欠拟合；若二者差距较大，则暗示过拟合。此外，早停（Early Stopping）通过监控验证集损失，在性能恶化前终止训练，是深度学习中常用的隐式正则化手段。

总体而言，过拟合与欠拟合并非孤立问题，而是与数据规模、噪声水平、模型复杂度及优化策略密切相关。通过在模型能力与数据约束之间取得平衡，结合系统性的验证与正则化手段，才能获得具有良好泛化能力的学习模型。

# 语音识别技术说明

语音识别（Automatic Speech Recognition，ASR）是将人类语音转换为可处理文本的技术，广泛应用于人机交互领域。

## 核心概念
- **语音信号采集**：通过麦克风等设备获取音频数据  
- **特征提取**：从语音中提取有代表性的声学特征  
- **声学模型**：将语音特征映射为音素或字词概率  
- **语言模型**：根据上下文预测最合理的词序列  

## 主要应用
- **智能语音助手**：如语音搜索、语音控制  
- **实时转写**：会议记录、字幕生成  
- **无障碍技术**：辅助听障或行动不便人群  

## 技术挑战
- **噪声干扰**：复杂环境下识别准确率下降  
- **口音与方言**：语音多样性带来的建模难度  
- **实时性要求**：需要在低延迟下完成识别  

## 发展趋势
- **深度学习模型**：提升识别准确率  
- **端到端系统**：简化传统多模块流程  
- **多语言支持**：实现跨语言语音识别

在实现方案上，模型服务化通常采用微服务架构，将模型推理与数据预处理、业务逻辑解耦。常见做法包括使用RESTful API或gRPC对外暴露推理接口，通过Docker和Kubernetes实现模型服务的容器化与弹性伸缩。在推理层面，可结合模型压缩、批量推理、异步调用等技术优化性能；在工程层面，则需要引入模型版本管理、灰度发布、在线监控和自动回滚机制，以保障服务的稳定性和可维护性。

从效果上看，模型服务化显著降低了模型上线和迭代的成本，使算法研发与业务系统形成清晰分工，提高了整体研发效率。同时，通过统一的服务接口和运维体系，模型能力可以被多个应用复用，避免重复开发。总体而言，模型服务化是连接算法研究与工程落地的关键桥梁，也是构建规模化智能系统的重要基础。

due to its high curie temperature and strong magnetic anisotropy , mnbi has attracted increasing attention in the pursuit of rare - earth - free permanent magnets ( see for example the review by poudyal and liu @xcite ) . 
 advances in the understanding of the properties and processing of this material continue , despite its relatively simple , nias - type crystal structure , and the fact that ferromagnetism in mnbi was first reported over a century ago @xcite . 
 key early studies were preformed by guillaud @xcite . in the 1950 s , 
 this material was considered as a candidate to replace permanent magnets containing cobalt and nickel , and an energy product of 4.3 mgoe was achieved in the resulting `` bismanol '' magnets @xcite . 
 subsequently , energy products as high as 7.7 mgoe have been reported @xcite . 
 mnbi has several promising aspects as a candidate replacement for rare earth magnets . 
 these include : ( 1 ) relatively inexpensive components @xcite , ( 2 ) high ordered moment and saturation magnetization of 0.58 ma m@xmath1 or about 3.5 @xmath2 per mn at room temperature @xcite , ( 3 ) ferromagnetism that persists to 630 k ( about 40 k higher than nd@xmath3fe@xmath4b ) @xcite , ( 4 ) large and uniaxial magnetocrystalline anisotropy energy near 1 mj m@xmath5 at room temperature ( moments along the c - axis ) , which increases upon heating above room temperature @xcite . 
 the observed increase in magnetic anisotropy and coercivity with increasing temperature is perhaps the most interesting , unique , and potentially important property of mnbi . 
 the ferromagnetism in mnbi vanishes abruptly upon heating above 630 k @xcite . 
 importantly , the phase transition that occurs near 630 k is not a typical magnetic transition . 
 this is not technically the curie temperature , and the transition is not directly driven by magnetism . 
 this transitions has been identified as a peritectic decomposition of mnbi .

 effects on the transport and anisotropic magnetic properties of the single crystals are also presented .

instruction: 用三段式结构（引言、正文、结论）介绍边缘计算。
output:
<think>\n\n</think>\n\n**引言**  
随着物联网、人工智能和5G等技术的快速发展，海量数据在网络边缘不断产生，传统依赖云计算的集中式处理模式逐渐暴露出时延高、带宽压力大等问题。在这样的背景下，边缘计算作为一种新的计算范式应运而生，受到广泛关注。

**正文**  
边缘计算是指将数据的计算、存储和分析能力从远端云数据中心下沉到靠近数据源的网络边缘节点，如传感器、网关或本地服务器。通过在数据产生的附近进行处理，边缘计算能够显著降低网络时延，减少数据传输量，提高系统的实时性和可靠性。这一技术在智能制造、自动驾驶、智慧城市和工业互联网等场景中具有重要应用价值。

**结论**  
总体来看，边缘计算是对云计算的重要补充，而非替代。它通过“就近计算”的方式解决了实时性和效率问题，为新一代智能应用提供了关键支撑。随着相关技术和标准的不断成熟，边缘计算将在未来的信息技术体系中发挥越来越重要的作用。

instruction: Help me translate this technical content to Chinese.
input: Model compression and quantization techniques are critical for deploying deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments by reducing model size, memory footprint, and inference latency while preserving accuracy. Model compression encompasses a spectrum of methods, including unstructured and structured pruning to remove redundant weights or channels, low-rank matrix factorization to exploit parameter redundancy, weight sharing and Huffman coding for entropy reduction, and knowledge distillation, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the soft targets of a larger teacher network. Quantization further improves efficiency by representing weights and activations with reduced numerical precision, such as INT8 or even INT4, instead of 32-bit floating point. Common approaches include post-training quantization, which applies quantization after model training using calibration data, and quantization-aware training (QAT), which simulates quantization effects during training to mitigate accuracy degradation. Advanced schemes leverage per-channel quantization, mixed-precision arithmetic, and symmetric or asymmetric scaling to better handle activation distributions and outliers. From a systems perspective, these techniques significantly reduce memory bandwidth requirements and energy consumption, and they align well with modern hardware accelerators that provide optimized integer arithmetic units. However, achieving an optimal accuracy–efficiency trade-off requires careful consideration of error propagation, activation clipping strategies, and hardware-specific constraints, making model compression and quantization an active area of research and engineering.

在大规模语言模型（LLM）广泛应用的背景下，如何稳定、高效地引导模型生成符合预期的输出成为核心问题。由于模型具有概率生成和上下文敏感的特性，简单的自然语言指令往往导致结果不确定、语义漂移或幻觉（hallucination）。Prompt Engineering 正是为解决人机交互中指令不精确、目标不可控而提出的一种系统化方法。

在方法层面，Prompt Engineering 通过结构化设计输入提示来约束模型行为。常见技术包括指令型提示（Instruction Prompting）、少样本提示（Few-shot Learning）、角色设定（Role Prompting）以及思维链提示（Chain-of-Thought）。此外，还可结合参数控制，如 temperature、top-k、max tokens 等，平衡生成的多样性与确定性。在复杂任务中，往往采用分步推理、显式约束输出格式，或结合外部工具与检索增强生成（RAG），以提升事实一致性和可解释性。

从效果上看，合理的 Prompt Engineering 能在无需重新训练模型的前提下显著提升任务性能，包括代码生成准确率、信息抽取稳定性以及多轮对话的上下文一致性。实践表明，该方法在成本、灵活性和快速迭代方面具有明显优势，已成为连接通用模型能力与具体业务需求的关键技术。随着模型规模和对齐技术的发展，Prompt Engineering 也正从经验驱动逐步走向方法论和工程化体系。

 the fermi surface ( fs ) partially remains even in the cdw phase due to the imperfect opening of the energy gap . 
 the origin of the cdw phase is still controversial and the usual nesting mechanism seems unlikely due to its poor fs nesting  @xcite . 
 alternatively , exciton condensation has been proposed as a possible mechanism for the cdw phase  @xcite . 
 indeed , the large spectral weight transfer between ti 3@xmath4 and se 4@xmath5 bands and the flat energy spectrum just below the fermi energy have been observed  @xcite , strongly suggesting the possibility of exciton condensation . on the other hand ,

instruction: 用简洁的语言概括下文的主要观点。
input:
Document summarization aims to automatically generate a concise and informative representation of one or more documents while preserving the core semantics. The problem arises from the rapid growth of digital text in domains such as scientific publishing, legal analysis, and enterprise knowledge management, where manual review is costly and inefficient. Effective summarization systems must balance information coverage, coherence, and factual consistency, while adapting to diverse document lengths, structures, and writing styles.

From a methodological perspective, document summarization is commonly categorized into extractive and abstractive approaches. Extractive methods select salient sentences or phrases directly from the source text based on features such as term frequency–inverse document frequency (TF‑IDF), graph-based centrality (e.g., TextRank), or supervised classifiers. While extractive summarization is relatively robust and preserves factual accuracy, it often suffers from redundancy and limited readability. In contrast, abstractive summarization generates novel sentences that paraphrase the source content, offering greater flexibility and coherence. Modern abstractive systems are typically built on sequence-to-sequence architectures with attention mechanisms, particularly transformer-based models that employ self-attention to capture long-range dependencies.

Recent advances in pre-trained language models have significantly improved summarization performance. Encoder–decoder transformers such as BART, T5, and PEGASUS leverage large-scale pretraining objectives, including denoising and gap-sentence prediction, to acquire strong semantic representations. Fine-tuning these models on domain-specific corpora enables adaptation to specialized vocabularies and discourse patterns. For long-document summarization, hierarchical encoders, sparse attention mechanisms, and chunking strategies are often introduced to overcome context-length limitations and reduce computational complexity.

Evaluation of document summarization remains a challenging aspect. Automatic metrics such as ROUGE, BLEU, and BERTScore are widely used to measure n-gram overlap or semantic similarity between generated summaries and reference summaries. However, these metrics correlate imperfectly with human judgment, especially for abstractive summaries. As a result, human evaluation criteria—such as relevance, coherence, fluency, and faithfulness—are still essential. Addressing factual hallucination, where generated content is not supported by the source document, has become a central research focus, motivating the integration of content planning, constrained decoding, and retrieval-augmented generation.

In conclusion, document summarization has evolved from heuristic-based extraction to sophisticated neural generation driven by large language models. While current systems achieve strong performance in many benchmarks, challenges remain in scalability, factual consistency, and domain generalization. Continued progress is expected through improved model architectures, better training objectives, and more reliable evaluation frameworks, making summarization an increasingly practical tool for managing large-scale textual information.

常见的量化方式包括后训练量化和量化感知训练。前者在模型训练完成后直接进行量化，实现简单；后者在训练阶段就考虑量化误差，通常能获得更好的精度表现。总体来看，模型量化是深度学习工程化和落地过程中一项重要技术。

instruction: 请提取以下论文片段的核心观点，并进行简要总结。
input:
Hallucination refers to the generation of factually incorrect, nonsensical, or unsupported content by large language models (LLMs), despite fluent and confident surface-level outputs. This phenomenon arises from the probabilistic nature of autoregressive generation, where models optimize next-token likelihood rather than factual correctness. Hallucinations pose significant risks in high-stakes applications such as medical decision support, legal analysis, and scientific research, undermining trust, safety, and downstream reliability. As model scale and deployment expand, hallucination mitigation has become a central research and engineering challenge in modern AI systems.

The root causes of hallucination are multifaceted. At the model level, pretraining on heterogeneous and noisy corpora induces spurious correlations and incomplete world representations. At inference time, exposure bias, prompt underspecification, and distribution shift can exacerbate overconfident errors. Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), while improving alignment and helpfulness, may unintentionally encourage persuasive but unverifiable responses. Additionally, parametric memory limitations prevent LLMs from reliably storing and recalling long-tail or rapidly evolving facts, leading to fabricated details when knowledge gaps are encountered.

A range of mitigation strategies has been proposed across the model lifecycle. Data-centric approaches include improved dataset curation, factuality-aware filtering, and synthetic data augmentation with verifiable ground truth. Model-centric methods focus on architectural and objective modifications, such as uncertainty-aware decoding, calibrated confidence estimation, and loss functions that penalize factual inconsistency. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has emerged as a particularly effective paradigm, grounding model outputs in external knowledge bases or search results and enabling explicit citation of sources. By conditioning generation on retrieved evidence, RAG reduces reliance on parametric memory and improves factual precision.

At inference time, decoding and control techniques further mitigate hallucinations. Constrained decoding, tool use, and function calling restrict the output space to valid actions or verified facts. Self-consistency, chain-of-thought verification, and self-reflection mechanisms allow models to detect and revise erroneous intermediate reasoning. Post-generation validation, including rule-based checkers, symbolic verifiers, or secondary critic models, provides an additional safeguard layer. Human-in-the-loop workflows remain critical in sensitive domains, combining automated checks with expert oversight.

Empirical evaluations demonstrate that these methods can significantly reduce hallucination rates, though trade-offs remain between latency, cost, and coverage. No single technique fully eliminates hallucinations, suggesting that robust solutions require system-level integration of multiple defenses. instruction: Translate the following CS paper abstract into Chinese.
input: The training of large language models (LLMs) typically follows a multi-stage pipeline that combines large-scale self-supervised learning with subsequent alignment techniques. In the pretraining phase, models based on the Transformer architecture are optimized on massive corpora of text using autoregressive or masked language modeling objectives, enabling them to learn general linguistic, syntactic, and semantic representations. This stage relies heavily on high-quality data curation, subword tokenization methods such as Byte Pair Encoding or SentencePiece, and large-batch stochastic gradient descent variants (e.g., AdamW) executed in distributed computing environments with data, model, and pipeline parallelism. Scaling laws guide decisions regarding model size, dataset size, and compute budget to achieve optimal performance. After pretraining, LLMs often undergo supervised fine-tuning on task-specific or instruction-following datasets to improve controllability and usability. More advanced alignment is achieved through Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), where a reward model trained on human preference data is used to further optimize the policy via algorithms such as Proximal Policy Optimization. Throughout training, regularization techniques, mixed-precision computation, and checkpointing are employed to ensure numerical stability and efficiency. Collectively, these methods enable LLMs to generalize across a wide range of downstream tasks while maintaining robustness and alignment with human expectations.
